sentences.zh: 上詔百官議其事，唯太僕卿張道源稱奕言合理。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered all officials to discuss the matter; only Grand Master of the Stables Zhang Daoyuan said Yi's words were reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all officials to discuss the matter; only Grand Master of the Stables Zhang Daoyuan said Yi's argument was sound.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀曰：「佛，聖人也，而奕非之；

translations.literal: Xiao Yu said: "The Buddha is a sage, yet Yi denounces him;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu said, "The Buddha is a sage, yet Yi denounces him;

sentences.zh: 非聖人者無法，當治其罪。」

translations.literal: He who denounces a sage is without law—he ought to be punished for his crime."
translations.idiomatic: He who denounces a sage is lawless and ought to be punished."

sentences.zh: 奕曰：「人之大倫，莫如君父。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Among human great bonds, none surpasses lord and father.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yi said, "Among the great bonds of humanity, none surpasses lord and father.

sentences.zh: 佛以世嫡而叛其父，以匹夫而抗天子。

translations.literal: The Buddha, as heir apparent of a generation, rebelled against his father; as a common man he resisted Heaven's Son.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha, as heir apparent of his age, rebelled against his father; as a common man he defied the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀不生於空桑，乃遵無父之教。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu was not born from a hollow mulberry tree, yet he follows a teaching without a father.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu was not born from a hollow mulberry tree, yet he follows a teaching that knows no father.

sentences.zh: 非孝者無親，瑀之謂矣！」

translations.literal: He who is not filial is without kin—this is Yu!"
translations.idiomatic: He who is unfilial is without kin—that is Yu!"

sentences.zh: 瑀不能對，但合手曰：「地獄之設，正為是人！」

translations.literal: Yu could not reply, but only joined his palms: "The hells were established precisely for such a person!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu could not answer, but only joined his palms and said, "Hell was made precisely for such a man!"

sentences.zh: 上亦惡沙門、道士苟避征徭，不守戒律，皆如奕言。

translations.literal: The emperor also detested Buddhist monks and Daoist priests who shirked levies and service, not keeping their precepts—all as Yi said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also detested Buddhist monks and Daoist priests who shirked levies and corvée and did not keep their precepts—all as Yi had said.

sentences.zh: 又寺觀鄰接廛邸，混雜屠沽。

translations.literal: Moreover temples and abbeys adjoined market wards, mixing with butchers and wine sellers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, temples and abbeys stood beside market wards, mingling with butchers and wine sellers.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，下詔命有司沙汰天下僧、尼、道士、女冠，其精勤練行者，遷居大寺觀，給其衣食，無令闕乏。

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict ordered the responsible offices to sift and purge monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and female Daoists throughout the realm; those diligent and practiced in cultivation were to be moved to great temples and abbeys, supplied with food and clothing, not allowed to lack.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, an edict ordered the authorities to purge monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and female Daoists throughout the realm; those diligent in practice were to be moved to major temples and abbeys and provided food and clothing so that nothing was lacking.

sentences.zh: 庸猥粗穢者，悉令罷道，勒還鄉里。

translations.literal: The mediocre, base, coarse, and filthy were all ordered to leave the Way and were compelled to return to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: The mediocre, coarse, and unclean were all ordered to leave the clergy and were compelled to return to their home districts.

sentences.zh: 京師留寺三所，觀二所，諸州各留一所，餘皆罷之。

translations.literal: In the capital three temples were retained, two abbeys; each prefecture retained one; the rest were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital three temples and two abbeys were retained; each prefecture kept one establishment; all the rest were abolished.

sentences.zh: 傅奕性謹密，既職在占候，杜絕交遊，所奏災異，悉焚其稿，人無知者。

translations.literal: Fu Yi's nature was cautious and secretive; once in charge of observing omens, he cut off social contact; whatever calamities and portents he reported, he burned all drafts—no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yi was cautious and secretive by nature; once charged with observing omens, he cut off all social contact; whatever calamities and portents he reported, he burned every draft, so that no one knew.

sentences.zh: 癸未，突厥寇西會州。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Turks raided West Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, the Turks raided West Hui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊子，虔州胡成郎等殺長史，叛歸梁師都；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuzi, Hu Cheng Lang and others of Qianzhou killed the chief clerk and rebelled, returning to Liang Shidu;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuzi, Hu Cheng Lang and others of Qian Prefecture killed the chief clerk and rebelled, going over to Liang Shidu;

sentences.zh: 都督劉旻追斬之。

translations.literal: Area commander Liu Min pursued and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Area commander Liu Min pursued and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，党項寇廓州。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Qiang tribes raided Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the Qiang tribes raided Kuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，突厥寇秦州。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Turks raided Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the Turks raided Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，越州人盧南反，殺刺史寧道明。

translations.literal: On renyin, Lu Nan of Yuezhou rebelled and killed Prefect Ning Daoming.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Lu Nan of Yue Prefecture rebelled and killed Prefect Ning Daoming.

sentences.zh: 丙午，吐谷渾、党項寇河州。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Tuyuhun and the Qiang tribes raided Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Tuyuhun and the Qiang tribes raided He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇蘭州。

translations.literal: The Turks raided Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks raided Lan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，遣平道將軍柴紹將兵擊胡。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the court sent General of the Level Road Chai Shao to lead troops and attack the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, the court sent General of the Level Road Chai Shao to lead troops against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁巳，太白經天。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingsi, Taibai crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingsi, the planet Venus crossed the heavens.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民既與太子建成、齊王元吉有隙，以洛陽形勝之地，恐一朝有變，欲出保之，乃以行台工部尚書溫大雅鎮洛陽，遣秦府車騎將軍滎陽張亮將左右王保等千餘人之洛陽，陰結納山東豪傑以俟變，多出金帛，恣其所用。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Shimin, having a rift with Crown Prince Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Yuanji, because Luoyang was a place of strategic terrain, feared that in one morning there might be change and wished to go out and secure it; he therefore had route-area Works Minister Wen Daya garrison Luoyang and sent Qin Palace Cavalry General of Xingyang Zhang Liang to lead Wang Bao and others of the personal guard, more than a thousand men, to Luoyang, secretly joining and winning over the powerful families of east of the mountains to await change, mostly disbursing gold and silk as they pleased to use.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Li Shimin, having fallen out with Crown Prince Li Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, regarded Luoyang as a place of strategic strength and feared that trouble might come at any moment; he wished to go out and secure it. He therefore stationed route-area Works Minister Wen Daya at Luoyang and sent Qin Palace Cavalry General Zhang Liang of Xingyang to lead Wang Bao and more than a thousand of his personal guard to Luoyang, secretly winning over the powerful families east of the mountains to await events, spending gold and silk freely as they saw fit.

sentences.zh: 元吉告亮謀不軌，下吏考驗；

translations.literal: Yuanji reported that Liang plotted irregularity; he was handed to officials for examination;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji reported that Zhang Liang was plotting sedition, and he was handed over to the authorities for interrogation;

sentences.zh: 亮終無言，乃釋之，使還洛陽。

translations.literal: Liang in the end said nothing; he was then released and sent back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang said nothing to the end; he was then released and sent back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 建成夜召世民，飲酒而鴆之，世民暴心痛，吐血數升，淮安王神通扶之還西宮。

translations.literal: Jiancheng summoned Shimin by night, drinking wine and poisoning him; Shimin suddenly suffered violent heart pain and spat blood several sheng; Prince of Huai'an Shen Tong supported him back to the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng summoned Shimin at night for wine and poisoned him; Shimin was seized with violent heart pain and vomited several sheng of blood; Prince of Huai'an Li Shen Tong helped him back to the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 上幸西宮，問世民疾，敕建成曰：「秦王素不能飲，自今無得復夜飲！」

translations.literal: The emperor visited the Western Palace, inquired after Shimin's illness, and charged Jiancheng: "Prince of Qin has never been able to drink—from now on he must not drink wine again at night!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited the Western Palace and inquired after Shimin's illness, then charged Jiancheng, "Prince of Qin has never been able to hold his wine—from now on he must not drink with him at night again!"

sentences.zh: 因謂世民曰：「首建大謀，削平海內，皆汝之功。

translations.literal: He then said to Shimin: "You were first to raise the great plan and level the seas within—all are your achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Shimin, "You were first to raise the great plan and pacify the realm within the seas—all of that is your achievement.

sentences.zh: 吾欲立汝為嗣，汝固辭；

translations.literal: I wished to establish you as heir, yet you firmly declined;
translations.idiomatic: I wished to make you my heir, but you firmly declined;

sentences.zh: 且建成年長，為嗣日久，吾不忍奪也。

translations.literal: Moreover Jiancheng is older, long established as heir—I cannot bear to displace him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Jiancheng is the elder and has long been heir—I cannot bear to displace him.

sentences.zh: 觀汝兄弟似不相容，同處京邑，必有紛競，當遣汝還行台，居洛陽，自陝以東皆王之。

translations.literal: Seeing that you brothers seem incompatible, dwelling together in the capital there will surely be strife and rivalry—I ought to send you back to the route-area, dwelling at Luoyang; from Shan eastward all shall be your kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that you brothers seem unable to get along, if you remain together in the capital there will surely be strife. I shall send you back to your route-area to dwell at Luoyang; from Shan eastward all shall be your domain.

sentences.zh: 仍命汝建天子旌旗，如漢梁孝王故事。」

translations.literal: He further ordered you to raise the Son of Heaven's banners, as in the precedent of Prince Xiao of Liang of Han."
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered that you raise the Son of Heaven's banners, following the precedent of Prince Xiao of Liang under the Han."

sentences.zh: 世民涕泣，辭以不欲遠離膝下。

translations.literal: Shimin wept, declining on the ground that he did not wish to be far from the emperor's knee.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin wept and declined on the ground that he did not wish to be far from his father's side.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「天下一家，東、西兩都，道路甚邇。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Under Heaven is one family; the eastern and western capitals—the road is very near.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "All under Heaven is one family; the eastern and western capitals lie very close together.

sentences.zh: 吾思汝即往，毋煩悲也。」

translations.literal: When I think of you I go at once—do not trouble yourself with grief."
translations.idiomatic: When I miss you I can go to you at once—do not grieve over it."

sentences.zh: 將行，建成、元吉相與謀曰：「秦王若至洛陽，有土地甲兵，不可復制；

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Jiancheng and Yuanji together plotted, saying: "If Prince of Qin reaches Luoyang, with territory and armor and troops, he cannot again be controlled;
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, Jiancheng and Yuanji plotted together, saying, "If Prince of Qin reaches Luoyang with land, armor, and troops, he will no longer be controllable;

sentences.zh: 不如留之長安，則一匹夫耳，取之易矣。」

translations.literal: It is better to keep him in Chang'an—then he is but a common fellow, and taking him will be easy."
translations.idiomatic: Better to keep him in Chang'an; then he is only a commoner, and easy to deal with."

sentences.zh: 乃密令數人上封事，言「秦王左右聞往洛陽，無不喜躍，觀其志趣，恐不復來。」

translations.literal: They thereupon secretly ordered several men to submit sealed memorials, saying: "Those about Prince of Qin, hearing of going to Luoyang, none are not joyful and leaping—observing their intent and will, I fear he will not return."
translations.idiomatic: They then secretly had several men submit sealed memorials stating, "Prince of Qin Li Shimin's attendants, hearing that he is to go to Luoyang, are all overjoyed; judging by their mood, he may never come back."

sentences.zh: 又遣近幸之臣以利害說上。

translations.literal: They also sent favored close ministers to persuade the emperor with advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent favored intimates to argue the pros and cons before Emperor Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 上意遂移，事復中止。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind thereupon shifted, and the matter again ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed his mind, and the plan was called off again.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉與後宮日夜譖訴世民於上，上信之，將罪世民。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji with the inner palace day and night slandered and accused Shimin before the emperor; the emperor believed them and was about to punish Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Li Jiancheng, Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, and the palace women slandered Li Shimin to Emperor Li Yuan day and night; the emperor believed them and was about to punish Shimin.

sentences.zh: 陳叔達諫曰：「秦王有大功於天下，不可黜也。

translations.literal: Chen Shuda remonstrated, saying: "Prince of Qin has great merit toward the realm—he cannot be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda remonstrated, saying, "Prince of Qin Li Shimin has rendered great service to the realm and must not be removed.

sentences.zh: 且性剛烈，若加挫抑，恐不勝憂憤，或有不測之疾，陛下悔之何及！」

translations.literal: Moreover his nature is stern and fierce; if you add setback and suppression, I fear he will not bear worry and anger—or there may be unforeseen illness—Your Majesty, when will regret catch up!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his nature is fierce; if you crush him further, he may not bear the grief and rage, or suffer some sudden illness—and then how will Your Majesty ever make amends!"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 元吉密請殺秦王，上曰：「彼有定天下之功，罪狀未著，何以為辭！」

translations.literal: Yuanji secretly requested killing Prince of Qin; the emperor said: "He has the merit of settling the realm; his crimes are not yet manifest—what shall be the plea!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji secretly asked that Prince of Qin be killed. The emperor said, "He helped settle the empire; no clear charge has been proved—what excuse could we give!"

sentences.zh: 元吉曰：「秦王初平東都，顧望不還，散錢帛以樹私恩，又違敕命，非反而何！

translations.literal: Yuanji said: "When Prince of Qin first pacified the eastern capital, he looked back and would not return, scattered money and silk to plant private favor, and again violated the imperial command—if not rebellion, what!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, "When Prince of Qin first pacified the eastern capital he lingered and would not return, scattered gold and silk to buy private loyalty, and defied your orders—if that is not treason, what is!

sentences.zh: 但應速殺，何患無辭！」

translations.literal: Only we ought quickly to kill—what worry is there of no plea!"
translations.idiomatic: Kill him at once—why worry about finding grounds!"

sentences.zh: 上不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 秦府僚屬皆憂懼不知所出。

translations.literal: The Qin Palace staff officials were all worried and afraid, not knowing what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: The staff of the Qin Palace were all anxious and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 行台考功郎中房玄齡謂比部郎中長孫無忌曰：「今嫌隙已成，一旦禍機竊發，豈惟府朝塗地，乃實社稷之憂；

translations.literal: Route-area Examination-of-Merit Bureau Director Fang Xuanling said to Revenue Bureau Director Changsun Wuji: "Now suspicion and rift are already formed; once calamity's trigger secretly breaks out, how is it only the palace court smeared to the ground—it is truly the altars of soil and grain's worry;
translations.idiomatic: Route-area Director of Examination of Merit Fang Xuanling said to Director of the Revenue Bureau Changsun Wuji, "The breach is already complete; once disaster strikes in secret, it will not be the Qin Palace alone that is ruined but the whole realm;

sentences.zh: 莫若勸王行周公之事以安家國。

translations.literal: None is better than urging the prince to perform the Duke of Zhou's affair to settle family and state.
translations.idiomatic: better to urge the prince to do what the Duke of Zhou did and secure the house and the state.

sentences.zh: 存亡之機，間不容髮，正在今日！」

translations.literal: Survival and destruction's pivot—between them no hair's breadth is tolerated—it is right in today!"
translations.idiomatic: Life and death hang by a hair—today is the day!"

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「吾懷此久矣，不敢發口；

translations.literal: Wuji said: "I have harbored this long, not daring to open the mouth;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "I have long felt this but dared not speak;

sentences.zh: 今吾子所言，正合吾心，謹當白之。」

translations.literal: what you, my lord, now say exactly fits my heart—I shall respectfully report it."
translations.idiomatic: what you say now is exactly my thought; I shall report it at once."

sentences.zh: 乃入言世民。

translations.literal: He then entered and spoke to Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: He then went in and told Shimin.

sentences.zh: 世民召玄齡謀之，玄齡曰：「大王功蓋天地，當承大業；

translations.literal: Shimin summoned Xuanling to plot; Xuanling said: "Great Prince, your merit covers heaven and earth—you ought to receive the great enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin summoned Fang Xuanling to counsel with him. Xuanling said, "Your Highness, your achievements overshadow heaven and earth; you should inherit the great enterprise;

sentences.zh: 今日憂危，乃天贊也，願大王勿疑！」

translations.literal: today's worry and peril is heaven's assistance—I wish the great prince not to doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: today's peril is heaven aiding you—do not doubt it!"

sentences.zh: 乃與府屬杜如晦共勸世民誅建成、元吉。

translations.literal: He then together with palace subordinate Du Ruhui jointly urged Shimin to execute Jiancheng and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: He and the palace officer Du Ruhui together urged Shimin to kill Jiancheng and Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉以秦府多驍將，欲誘之使為己用，密以金銀器一車贈左二副護軍尉遲敬德，並以書招之曰：「願迂長者之眷，以敦布衣之交。」

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji, because the Qin Palace had many fierce generals, wished to entice them to serve themselves; secretly with gold and silver vessels one cart they gifted Left Second Vice Protector of the Army Yuchi Jingde, and with a letter recruited him, saying: "We wish to turn aside the elder's regard, to thicken the plain-cloth friendship."
translations.idiomatic: Because the Qin Palace had many fierce commanders, Jiancheng and Yuanji tried to win them over, secretly sending a cartload of gold and silver vessels to Left Second Vice Protector of the Army Yuchi Jingde and a letter inviting him: "We hope you will extend your favor to us and renew the friendship of our common days."

sentences.zh: 敬德辭曰：「敬德，蓬戶甕牖之人，遭隋末亂離，久淪逆地，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: Jingde declined, saying: "Jingde is a man of wicker gate and earthen window—meeting Sui's end chaos and separation, long sunk in rebellious ground, crime not tolerating execution.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde declined, saying, "I am a man of humble gate and broken window; caught in the chaos at the end of Sui, I long dwelt among rebels and deserved death.

sentences.zh: 秦王賜以更生之恩，今又策名籓邸，唯當殺身以為報；

translations.literal: Prince of Qin bestowed the grace of renewed life; now again I have registered my name at the princely residence—only ought to give my body in return;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Li Shimin granted me a new life, and now I have pledged myself to his house; I can only repay him with my life;

sentences.zh: 於殿下無功，不敢謬當重賜。

translations.literal: toward Your Highness I have no merit—I do not dare wrongly receive heavy gifts.
translations.idiomatic: I have done nothing for Your Highness and dare not accept such rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 若私交殿下，乃是貳心，徇利忘忠，殿下亦何所用！」

translations.literal: If I privately befriend Your Highness, that is divided heart, following profit and forgetting loyalty—what use has Your Highness!"
translations.idiomatic: If I kept a private tie with Your Highness, that would be divided loyalty—selling honor for gain. Of what use would I be to you!"

sentences.zh: 建成怒，遂與之絕。

translations.literal: Jiancheng was angry and thereupon broke with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng was furious and broke with him.

sentences.zh: 敬德以告世民，世民曰：「公心如山嶽，雖積金至鬥，知公不移。

translations.literal: Jingde reported it to Shimin; Shimin said: "Your lordship's heart is like mountains and peaks—though gold piled to a bushel, I know you do not shift.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde told Shimin. Shimin said, "Your heart is immovable as a mountain; though they heaped gold by the bushel, I knew you would not waver.

sentences.zh: 相遺但受，何所嫌也！

translations.literal: Their gift—only receive it—what is there to dislike!
translations.idiomatic: Take whatever they send—why refuse!

sentences.zh: 且得以知其陰計，豈非良策！

translations.literal: Moreover we can thereby know their secret schemes—is that not a fine stratagem!
translations.idiomatic: We can learn their secret designs—is that not the better plan!

sentences.zh: 不然，禍將及公。」

translations.literal: If not, calamity will reach you, lord."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise disaster will reach you."

sentences.zh: 既而元吉使壯士夜刺敬德，敬德知之，洞開重門，安臥不動，刺客屢至其庭，終不敢入。

translations.literal: Before long Yuanji sent stalwart men by night to stab Jingde; Jingde knew it, opened wide the layered gates, lay peacefully without moving—the assassins repeatedly came to his courtyard, in the end not daring to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuanji sent bravos to stab Jingde by night. Jingde knew of it, threw open his inner gates, and lay still; the assassins came again and again to his courtyard but never dared enter.

sentences.zh: 元吉乃譖敬德於上，下詔獄訊治，將殺之。

translations.literal: Yuanji then slandered Jingde before the emperor; an edict sent him to prison for interrogation and punishment, about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji then slandered Jingde to the emperor, who ordered him imprisoned and interrogated, intending to execute him.

sentences.zh: 世民固請，得免。

translations.literal: Shimin firmly requested, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin pleaded hard and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 又譖左一馬軍總管程知節，出為康州刺史。

translations.literal: Again they slandered Left First Cavalry Army Commander-in-Chief Cheng Zhijie, who was sent out as Kang Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: They also slandered Left First Cavalry Army Commander-in-Chief Cheng Zhijie, who was sent out as prefect of Kang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知節謂世民曰：「大王股肱羽翼盡矣，身何能久！

translations.literal: Zhijie said to Shimin: "Great Prince, your arms and thighs and wings are all gone—how can the body long endure!
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie said to Shimin, "Your Highness, your arms and wings are all gone—how can you last!

sentences.zh: 知節以死不去，願早決計。」

translations.literal: Zhijie with death will not leave—I wish early settled plans."
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie will not leave you even at the cost of his life; decide soon."

sentences.zh: 又以金帛誘右二護軍段志玄，志玄不從。

translations.literal: Again with gold and silk they enticed Right Second Protector of the Army Duan Zhixuan; Zhixuan did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: They also tried to buy Right Second Protector of the Army Duan Zhixuan with gold and silk; Zhixuan refused.

sentences.zh: 建成謂元吉曰：「秦府智略之士，可憚者獨房玄齡、杜如晦耳。」

translations.literal: Jiancheng said to Yuanji: "Among the Qin Palace's men of strategy and counsel, those to be feared are only Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui."
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng said to Yuanji, "Of the Qin Palace's strategists, only Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui need be feared."

sentences.zh: 皆譖之於上而逐之。

translations.literal: Both slandered them before the emperor and expelled them.
translations.idiomatic: They slandered both to the emperor and had them dismissed.

sentences.zh: 世民腹心唯長孫無忌尚在府中，與其舅雍州治中高士廉、左候車騎將軍三水侯君集及尉遲敬德等，日夜勸世民誅建成、元吉。

translations.literal: Of Shimin's trusted inner circle only Changsun Wuji still remained in the palace, together with his maternal uncle Yong Prefecture Administrator Gao Shilian, Left Waiting Cavalry-and-Chariot General Sanshui Hou Junji, and Yuchi Jingde and others—day and night urging Shimin to execute Jiancheng and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Of Shimin's inner circle only Changsun Wuji still remained in the palace, together with his uncle Yong Prefecture Administrator Gao Shilian, Left Waiting Cavalry-and-Chariot General Hou Junji of Sanshui, Yuchi Jingde, and others, who night and day urged Shimin to kill Jiancheng and Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 世民猶豫未決，問於靈州大都督李靖，靖辭；

translations.literal: Shimin hesitated and had not decided; he asked Lingzhou Grand Area Commander Li Jing—Jing declined;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin still hesitated. He asked Lingzhou Grand Area Commander Li Jing; Jing declined to answer;

sentences.zh: 問於行軍總管李世勣，世勣辭；

translations.literal: he asked Campaigning Army Commander-in-Chief Li Shiji—Shiji declined;
translations.idiomatic: he asked Campaigning Army Commander-in-Chief Li Shiji; Shiji also declined;

sentences.zh: 世民由是重二人。

translations.literal: Shimin thereby valued the two men.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin therefore esteemed both men the more.

sentences.zh: 會突厥郁射設將數萬騎屯河南，入塞，圍烏城，建成薦元吉代世民督諸軍北征；

translations.literal: It happened that the Türk Yushishe led several tens of thousands of horsemen encamped south of the Yellow River, entered the frontier, and besieged Wucheng; Jiancheng recommended Yuanji replace Shimin in commanding the various armies on the northern campaign;
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Türk leader Yushishe camped south of the Yellow River with tens of thousands of horsemen, crossed the border, and besieged Wucheng. Jiancheng recommended that Yuanji replace Shimin in commanding the northern armies;

sentences.zh: 上從之，命元吉督右武衛大將軍李藝、天紀將軍張瑾等救烏城。

translations.literal: the emperor followed it, ordering Yuanji to command Right Martial Guard General Li Yi, Heavenly Record General Zhang Jin, and others to rescue Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed and ordered Yuanji to command Right Martial Guard General Li Yi, Heavenly Record General Zhang Jin, and others to relieve Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 元吉請尉遲敬德、程知節、段志玄及秦府右三統軍秦叔寶等與之偕行，簡閱秦王帳下精銳之士以益元吉軍。

translations.literal: Yuanji requested Yuchi Jingde, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, and Qin Palace Right Third Commander Qin Shubao and others to go with him, selecting and reviewing the elite sharp troops under Prince of Qin's command to augment Yuanji's army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji asked that Yuchi Jingde, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, and Qin Palace Right Third Commander Qin Shubao accompany him, and picked the finest troops under Prince of Qin Li Shimin to strengthen Yuanji's force.

sentences.zh: 率更丞王晊密告世民曰：「太子語齊王：『今汝得秦王驍將精兵，擁數萬之眾，吾與秦王餞汝於昆明池，使壯士拉殺之於幕下，奏雲暴卒，主上宜無不信。

translations.literal: Directorate of Palace Revenues Registrar Wang Xi secretly reported to Shimin: "The crown prince said to Prince of Qi: 'Now you have obtained Prince of Qin's fierce generals and elite troops, holding several tens of thousands— I with Prince of Qin will send you off at Kunming Pool, have stalwart men strangle and kill him beneath the tent curtain, memorialize saying sudden death—the lord ought not disbelieve.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar of the Directorate for Palace Revenues Wang Xi secretly told Shimin, "The crown prince said to the Prince of Qi, 'Now that you have Prince of Qin Li Shimin's fierce commanders and elite troops, with tens of thousands at your back, he and I will give you a farewell feast at Kunming Pool and have bravos throttle him under the awning; we shall report that he died suddenly, and the emperor should not doubt it.

sentences.zh: 吾當使人進說，令授吾國事。

translations.literal: I shall send men to advance persuasion, ordering that state affairs be entrusted to me.
translations.idiomatic: I will send men to persuade him to hand the realm over to me.

sentences.zh: 敬德等既入汝手，宜悉坑之，孰敢不服！』」

translations.literal: Jingde and the rest, once in your hand, ought all to be buried alive—who dares not submit!'
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingde and the rest are in your hands, bury them all—who would dare resist!'

sentences.zh: 世民以咥言告長孫無忌等，無忌等勸世民先事圖之。

translations.literal: Shimin with Xi's words told Changsun Wuji and the rest; Wuji and the rest urged Shimin first to take affairs and plot.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin told Changsun Wuji and the others what Wang Xi had said; they urged him to strike first.

sentences.zh: 世民歎曰：「骨肉相殘，古今大惡。

translations.literal: Shimin sighed: "Flesh and bone mutually mutilating—through ancient and modern times a great evil.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin sighed and said, "Brothers tearing one another apart is the greatest evil in any age.

sentences.zh: 吾誠知禍在朝夕，欲俟其發，然後以義討之，不亦可乎！」

translations.literal: I truly know calamity is at dawn and dusk; I wish to wait until they act, then with righteousness punish them—is that not also acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: I know disaster is near, yet I wish to wait until they move and then punish them in the name of justice—is that not possible!"

sentences.zh: 敬德曰：「人情誰不愛其死！

translations.literal: Jingde said: "Among human feelings, who does not love his death!
translations.idiomatic: Jingde said, "Who does not cling to life!

sentences.zh: 今眾人以死奉王，乃天授也。

translations.literal: Now the multitude with death serve the prince—it is heaven's grant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now these men are ready to die for you—that is heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 禍機垂發，而王猶晏然不以為憂，大王縱自輕，如宗廟社稷何！

translations.literal: Calamity's trigger hangs about to break forth, yet the prince is still peaceful and untroubled, not taking it as worry—great prince, though you yourself may be light, what of the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: Disaster is about to break, yet Your Highness sits at ease as if unconcerned. Even if you hold your own life cheap, what of the altars of the realm!

sentences.zh: 大王不用敬德之言，敬德將竄身草澤，不能留居大王左右，交手受戮也！」

translations.literal: Great prince, if you do not use Jingde's words, Jingde will flee the body into grass and marsh, unable to remain dwelling at the great prince's left and right, crossing hands and receiving slaughter!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness will not heed me, I shall flee to the wilds rather than stay at your side to be butchered with folded hands!"

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「不從敬德之言，事今敗矣。

translations.literal: Wuji said: "If we do not follow Jingde's words, the affair is now defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "If we ignore Jingde, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 敬德等必不為王有，無忌亦當相隨而去，不能復事大王矣！」

translations.literal: Jingde and the rest surely will not remain the prince's to have; Wuji also ought to follow and leave, unable again to serve the great prince!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingde and the rest will no longer be yours; I too must leave and cannot serve you again!"

sentences.zh: 世民曰：「吾所言亦未可全棄，公更圖之。」

translations.literal: Shimin said: "What I said also cannot be wholly abandoned—my lords, plot again."
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said, "What I said is not wholly wrong either; think again."

sentences.zh: 敬德曰：「王今處事有疑，非智也；

translations.literal: Jingde said: "Prince, now in handling affairs you have doubt—that is not wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: Jingde said, "To doubt at the decisive moment is not wisdom;

sentences.zh: 臨難不決，非勇也。

translations.literal: facing peril and not deciding—that is not courage.
translations.idiomatic: to face peril and not decide is not courage.

sentences.zh: 且大王素所畜養勇士八百餘人，在外者今已入宮，擐甲執兵，事勢已成，大王安得已乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover the great prince's usual reared brave warriors are more than eight hundred; those outside now have entered the palace, donning armor and grasping weapons—the affair's momentum is already formed—how can the great prince stop!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the more than eight hundred warriors you have long kept are already in the palace in armor with weapons drawn—the deed is set in motion; how can Your Highness turn back!"

sentences.zh: 世民訪之府僚，皆曰：「齊王凶戾，終不肯事其兄。

translations.literal: Shimin inquired of the palace staff; all said: "Prince of Qi is fierce and cruel—he in the end will not be willing to serve his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin consulted his staff; all said, "Prince of Qi Li Yuanji is brutal and will never serve his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 比聞護軍薛實嘗謂齊王曰：『大王之名，合之成「唐」字，大王終主唐祀。』

translations.literal: Recently I heard Protector of the Army Xue Shi once said to Prince of Qi: 'Great prince's name, combined, forms the character "Tang"—the great prince in the end will master Tang's sacrifices.'
translations.idiomatic: We lately heard that Protector of the Army Xue Shi told the Prince of Qi, 'Your name, taken together, forms the character Tang—you are destined to rule the house of Tang.'

sentences.zh: 齊王喜曰：『但除秦王，取東宮如反掌耳。』

translations.literal: Prince of Qi rejoiced: 'Only remove Prince of Qin—taking the Eastern Palace is like turning the palm.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was delighted and said, 'Only remove Prince of Qin Li Shimin, and seizing the Eastern Palace is as easy as turning one's hand.'

sentences.zh: 彼與太子謀亂未成，已有取太子之心。

translations.literal: He with the crown prince plotted disorder not yet accomplished—already he had the mind to take the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He and the crown prince have not yet finished their plot, but he already means to supplant the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 亂心無厭，何所不為！

translations.literal: Disorder's heart without satiety—what would he not do!
translations.idiomatic: With such restless ambition, what would he not do!

sentences.zh: 若使二人得志，恐天下非復唐有。

translations.literal: If we let the two men realize their will, I fear the realm under heaven will no longer be Tang's to hold.
translations.idiomatic: If those two prevail, the realm may no longer belong to Tang.

sentences.zh: 以大王之賢，取二人如拾地芥耳，奈何徇匹夫之節，忘社稷之計乎！」

translations.literal: With the great prince's worth, taking the two men is like picking mustard seeds from the ground—why follow a common fellow's integrity and forget the altars of soil and grain's plans!"
translations.idiomatic: With Your Highness's worth, removing them is like picking seeds from the ground—why cling to private scruple and forget the state!"

sentences.zh: 世民猶未決，眾曰：「大王以舜為何如人？」

translations.literal: Shimin still had not decided; the multitude said: "Great prince, what sort of man do you take Shun to be?"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin still hesitated. They said, "What sort of man was Shun, in Your Highness's view?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「聖人也。」

translations.literal: He said: "A sage."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "A sage."

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「使舜浚井不出，則為井中之泥；

translations.literal: The multitude said: "If Shun dredging the well did not come out, then he would be mud in the well;
translations.idiomatic: They said, "If Shun had not escaped when they sent him down the well, he would be mud at the bottom;

sentences.zh: 塗廩不下，則為廩上之灰，安能澤被天下，法施後世乎！

translations.literal: smearing the granary and not descending, then he would be ash atop the granary—how could he extend grace over the realm and law reach later generations!
translations.idiomatic: if he had not fled when they set fire to the granary, he would be ashes on the roof—how could he have blessed the world and left his example to later ages!

sentences.zh: 是以小杖則受，大杖則走，蓋所存者大故也。」

translations.literal: Therefore with a small staff he accepted, with a large staff he ran—it was because what he preserved was great."
translations.idiomatic: That is why he accepted a light beating but fled a heavy one—because the greater good mattered."

sentences.zh: 世民命卜之，幕僚張公謹自外來，取龜投地，曰：「卜以決疑；

translations.literal: Shimin ordered divination; staff officer Zhang Gongjin came from outside, took the tortoise and cast it to the ground, saying: "Divination is to resolve doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin ordered divination. Staff officer Zhang Gongjin came in from outside, seized the tortoise, and threw it down, saying, "One divines to settle doubt;

sentences.zh: 今事在不疑，尚何卜乎！

translations.literal: now the affair is in no doubt—why still divine!
translations.idiomatic: there is no doubt now—why divine!

sentences.zh: 卜而不吉，庸得已乎！」

translations.literal: If you divine and it is not auspicious, how can you stop!"
translations.idiomatic: If the omen were ill, could you stop anyway!"

sentences.zh: 於是定計。

translations.literal: Thereupon the plan was settled.
translations.idiomatic: At that the decision was made.

sentences.zh: 世民令無忌密召房玄齡等，曰：「敕旨不聽復事王；

translations.literal: Shimin ordered Wuji secretly to summon Fang Xuanling and the rest; they said: "The imperial command does not permit again serving the prince;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin had Wuji secretly summon Fang Xuanling and the others. They said, "The edict forbids us to serve the prince again;

sentences.zh: 今若私謁，必坐死，不敢奉教。」

translations.literal: if now we privately visit, we will surely sit in death—we dare not receive the instruction."
translations.idiomatic: if we come in private we shall be put to death and dare not obey."

sentences.zh: 世民怒，謂敬德曰：「玄齡、如晦豈叛我邪！」

translations.literal: Shimin was angry and said to Jingde: "Xuanling and Ruhui—would they rebel against me!"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin was angry and said to Jingde, "Would Xuanling and Ruhui betray me!"

sentences.zh: 取所佩刀授敬德曰：「公往觀之，若無來心，可斷其首以來。」

translations.literal: He took the knife at his belt and gave it to Jingde: "My lord, go and observe; if they have no mind to come, you may cut off their heads and bring them."
translations.idiomatic: He took the sword at his belt and handed it to Jingde, saying, "Go and see; if they will not come, cut off their heads and bring them here."

sentences.zh: 敬德往，與無忌共諭之曰：「王已決計，公宜速入共謀之。

translations.literal: Jingde went, and together with Wuji jointly instructed them: "The prince has already settled the plan—you lords ought quickly to enter and plot together.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde went, and he and Wuji told them together, "The prince has made up his mind; come at once and counsel with him.

sentences.zh: 吾屬四人，不可群行道中。」

translations.literal: Our sort, four men—we cannot walk the road in a crowd."
translations.idiomatic: We four must not walk the streets together."

sentences.zh: 乃令玄齡、如晦著道士服，與無忌俱入，敬德自它道亦至。

translations.literal: He then ordered Xuanling and Ruhui to wear Taoist robes, and with Wuji all entered; Jingde by another road also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xuanling and Ruhui put on Taoist robes and enter with Wuji, while Jingde came by another route.

sentences.zh: 己未，太白復經天。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Taibai again crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Venus again crossed the heavens.

sentences.zh: 傅奕密奏：「太白見秦分，秦王當有天下。」

translations.literal: Fu Yi secretly memorialized: "Taibai appeared in Qin's division—Prince of Qin ought to have the realm under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yi secretly memorialized, "Venus has appeared in the Qin asterism—Prince of Qin Li Shimin is destined to rule the realm."

sentences.zh: 上以其狀授世民。

translations.literal: The emperor with his memorial handed it to Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave the memorial to Shimin.

sentences.zh: 於是世民密奏建成、元吉淫亂後宮，且曰：「臣于兄弟無絲毫負，今欲殺臣，似為世充、建德報仇。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shimin secretly memorialized that Jiancheng and Yuanji debauched the inner palace, and added: "Your subject toward brothers has not a thread or hair of failing—now they wish to kill your subject, as if avenging Shichong and Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin then secretly accused Jiancheng and Yuanji of debauching the inner palace, adding, "I have done my brothers no wrong, yet they would kill me—as if to avenge Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 臣今枉死，永違君親，魂歸地下，實恥見諸賊！」

translations.literal: Your subject now dies wrongfully, forever parting from lord and kin—soul returning beneath the ground, truly shamed to see the various villains!"
translations.idiomatic: If I die unjustly I shall never see my sovereign and kin again; my ghost in the underworld would be ashamed to meet those villains!"

sentences.zh: 上省之，愕然，報曰：「明當鞫問，汝宜早參。」

translations.literal: The emperor examined it, startled, and replied: "Tomorrow we shall interrogate and question—you ought early to attend court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it, stunned, and replied, "We shall investigate tomorrow; come early to court."

sentences.zh: 庚申，世民帥長孫無忌等入，伏兵於玄武門。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Shimin led Changsun Wuji and others in, and ambush troops at Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Shimin entered with Changsun Wuji and the others and posted ambush troops at Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 張婕妤竊知世民表意，馳語建成。

translations.literal: Consort Zhang secretly knew Shimin's memorial's intent and galloped to tell Jiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang secretly learned the purport of Shimin's memorial and raced to tell Jiancheng.

sentences.zh: 建成召元吉謀之，元吉曰：「宜勒宮府兵，托疾不朝，以觀形勢。」

translations.literal: Jiancheng summoned Yuanji to plot; Yuanji said: "We ought to order palace and residence troops, feign illness and not attend court, to observe the situation's form."
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng summoned Yuanji to counsel. Yuanji said, "We should muster the palace guards, plead illness, and stay away from court to see how matters stand."

sentences.zh: 建成曰：「兵備已嚴，當與弟入參，自問消息。」

translations.literal: Jiancheng said: "Arms and preparations are already strict—we ought with younger brother to enter and attend court, ourselves asking the news."
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng said, "Our forces are already ready; we should go in with you and attend court ourselves to learn what is afoot."

sentences.zh: 乃俱入，趣玄武門。

translations.literal: They then both entered, hastening to Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They both went in and hurried toward Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 上時已召裴寂、蕭瑀、陳叔達等，欲按其事。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had already summoned Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, and others, intending to investigate the affair.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had already summoned Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, and others to investigate the matter.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉至臨湖殿，覺變，即跋馬東歸宮府。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji reached Linhu Hall, sensed the change, and at once spurred their horses east back to the palace residences.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiancheng and Yuanji reached Linhu Hall and sensed trouble, they spurred their horses east back toward their residences.

sentences.zh: 世民從而呼之，元吉張弓射世民，再三不彀，世民射建成，殺之。

translations.literal: Shimin followed and called to them; Yuanji drew his bow and shot at Shimin, several times without drawing it fully; Shimin shot Jiancheng and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin pursued and called after them; Yuanji drew his bow and shot at Shimin but failed to draw it fully three times; Shimin shot Jiancheng and killed him.

sentences.zh: 尉遲敬德將七十騎繼至，左右射元吉墜馬。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jingde leading seventy riders came up after; those at left and right shot Yuanji and he fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde came up with seventy riders; men on either side shot Yuanji and knocked him from his horse.

sentences.zh: 世民馬逸入林下，為木枝所絓，墜不能起。

translations.literal: Shimin's horse bolted into the woods below, was snagged by a wooden branch, fell, and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin's horse bolted into the woods and was tangled by a branch; he fell and could not get up.

sentences.zh: 元吉遽至，奪弓將扼之，敬德躍馬叱之。

translations.literal: Yuanji suddenly arrived, seized the bow and was about to strangle him; Jingde leaped on his horse and shouted at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji rushed up, seized the bow, and was about to strangle him; Jingde spurred forward and shouted him down.

sentences.zh: 元吉步欲趣武德殿，敬德追射，殺之。

translations.literal: Yuanji on foot wished to hurry to Wude Hall; Jingde pursued and shot, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji fled on foot toward Wude Hall; Jingde pursued and shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 翊衛車騎將軍馮翊馮立聞建成死，歎曰：「豈有生受其恩，而死逃其難乎！」

translations.literal: Assistant Guard Cavalry General of Fufeng Feng Li, hearing Jiancheng was dead, sighed and said: "How can one in life receive his favor, yet in death flee his hardship!"
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Guard Cavalry General Feng Li of Fufeng, hearing that Jiancheng was dead, sighed and said, "How can one accept his grace in life and then flee his peril in death?"

sentences.zh: 乃與副護軍薛萬徹、屈咥直府左車騎萬年謝叔方帥東宮、齊府精兵二千馳趣玄武門。

translations.literal: He then with deputy protector Xue Wanche, Quzhi Directorate of the Palace Left Cavalry of Wannian Xie Shufang led two thousand picked troops of the Eastern Palace and Qi residence galloping to Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Deputy Protector Xue Wanche and Quzhi Palace Left Cavalry of Wannian Xie Shufang, led two thousand crack troops from the Eastern Palace and the Prince of Qi's residence, and raced for Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 張公謹多力，獨閉關以拒之，不得入。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongjian was very strong and alone closed the gate to resist them; they could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongjian, a man of great strength, alone barred the gate against them, and they could not get through.

sentences.zh: 雲麾將軍敬君弘掌宿衛後，屯玄武門，挺身出戰，所親止之曰：「事未可知，且徐觀變，俟兵集，成列而戰，未晚也。」

translations.literal: Cloud-Banner General Jing Junhong in charge of rear night guards was stationed at Xuanwu Gate; he stepped forward to fight; those close to him stopped him, saying: "The affair is not yet knowable; wait and observe the change slowly; when troops are gathered, form ranks and fight—it is not yet late."
translations.idiomatic: Cloud-Banner General Jing Junhong, who commanded the rear night guard, was posted at Xuanwu Gate. He stepped forward to fight, but those close to him urged, "The situation is still unclear; watch how matters unfold, wait until our troops are gathered, and fight in formation—you will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 君弘不從，與中郎將呂世衡大呼而進，皆死之。

translations.literal: Junhong would not heed; with mid-level general Lü Shiheng he shouted and advanced; both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Junhong would not listen; he and Mid-Level General Lü Shiheng charged forward shouting, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 君弘，顯俊之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Junhong was the great-grandson of Xianjun.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Junhong was a great-grandson of Jing Xianjun.

sentences.zh: 守門兵與萬徹等力戰良久，萬徹鼓噪欲攻秦府，將士大懼；

translations.literal: The gate-guard troops and Wanche and others fought fiercely for a long time; Wanche beat drums and clamored, intending to attack the Prince of Qin's residence; officers and soldiers were greatly afraid;
translations.idiomatic: The gate guards battled Xue Wanche's men for a long time; Wanche raised a din and prepared to assault the Prince of Qin's residence, and the troops were deeply alarmed;

sentences.zh: 尉遲敬德持建成、元吉首示之，宮府兵遂潰，萬徹與數十騎亡入終南山。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jingde held up Jiancheng's and Yuanji's heads to show them; the palace residence troops thereupon scattered; Wanche with several tens of riders fled into Zhongnan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde raised the heads of Jiancheng and Yuanji for all to see; the Eastern Palace and Qi residence troops broke and fled; Wanche escaped into the Zhongnan Mountains with several dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 馮立既殺敬君弘，謂其徒曰：「亦足以少報太子矣！」

translations.literal: Feng Li, having killed Jing Junhong, said to his followers: "This too is enough to repay the crown prince a little!"
translations.idiomatic: After Feng Li had killed Jing Junhong, he told his men, "That is repayment enough for the crown prince!"

sentences.zh: 遂解兵，逃於野。

translations.literal: He then dismissed the troops and fled into the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: He then disbanded his force and fled into the countryside.

sentences.zh: 上方泛舟海池，世民使尉遲敬德入宿衛，敬德擐甲持矛，直至上所。

translations.literal: The emperor was then boating on the Sea Pond; Shimin had Yuchi Jingde enter as night guard; Jingde donned armor and took a spear, going straight to where the emperor was.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then boating on the imperial pond; Shimin sent Yuchi Jingde in as night guard; Jingde came in full armor with spear in hand straight to the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 上大驚，問曰：「今日亂者誰邪？

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly startled and asked: "Who is rioting today?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly startled and asked, "Who has risen in revolt today?

sentences.zh: 卿來此何為？」

translations.literal: Why have you come here?"
translations.idiomatic: Why have you come here?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「秦王以太子、齊王作亂，舉兵誅之，恐驚動陛下，遣臣宿衛。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The Prince of Qin, because the crown prince and Prince of Qi made rebellion, raised troops to execute them; fearing to startle Your Majesty, he sent me to stand night guard."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The Prince of Qin, learning that the crown prince and Prince of Qi had rebelled, took up arms to punish them; fearing to alarm Your Majesty, he sent me to guard you."

sentences.zh: 上謂裴寂等曰：「不圖今日乃見此事，當如之何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Pei Ji and others: "I never expected to see this affair today—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Pei Ji and the others, "I never thought to see this in my lifetime—what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀、陳叔達曰：「建成、元吉本不預義謀，又無功於天下，疾秦王功高望重，共為奸謀。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu and Chen Shuda said: "Jiancheng and Yuanji from the first did not join the righteous planning, and again had no achievement for the realm; they resented the Prince of Qin's achievements high and renown heavy, and together made treacherous plots.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu and Chen Shuda said, "Jiancheng and Yuanji were never party to founding the dynasty and had no great deeds to their credit; jealous of the Prince of Qin's towering merit, they plotted together.

sentences.zh: 今秦王已討而誅之，秦王功蓋宇宙，率土歸心，陛下若處以元良，委之國務，無復事矣。」

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Qin has already punished and executed them; the Prince of Qin's achievements cover heaven and earth, all within the seas turn their hearts to him—if Your Majesty would place him as heir apparent and entrust state affairs to him, there would be nothing more to do."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin has already punished them. His merit fills heaven and earth and the realm turns to him; if Your Majesty would name him heir and entrust him with state affairs, nothing more need be done."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said!

sentences.zh: 此吾之夙心也。」

translations.literal: This is my long-standing heart."
translations.idiomatic: That has long been my own wish."

sentences.zh: 時宿衛及秦府兵與二宮左右戰猶未已，敬德請降手敕，令諸軍並受秦王處分，上從之。

translations.literal: At that time night guards and Prince of Qin residence troops with the two palaces' attendants were still fighting and not yet ended; Jingde requested a lowered hand edict ordering all armies alike to accept the Prince of Qin's disposal; the emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting still raged between the palace guards, the Prince of Qin's troops, and the retainers of the two palaces; Jingde asked for an edict in the emperor's own hand placing all forces under the Prince of Qin's command, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 天策府司馬宇文士及自東上閣門出宣敕，眾然後定。

translations.literal: Heavenly Stratagem headquarters marshal Yuwen Shiji from the Upper Eastern Tower Gate came out to proclaim the edict; the masses then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly Stratagem Marshal Yuwen Shiji proclaimed the edict from the Upper Eastern Tower Gate, and only then did the troops calm down.

sentences.zh: 上又使黃門侍郎裴矩至東宮曉諭諸將卒，皆罷散。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Yellow Gate vice-director Pei Ju to the Eastern Palace to dawn-instruct the various generals and soldiers; all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Yellow Gate Vice-Director Pei Ju to the Eastern Palace to explain matters to the officers and men, and they all dispersed.

sentences.zh: 上乃召世民，撫之曰：「近日以來，幾有投杼之惑。」

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned Shimin, stroked him and said: "In recent days there was nearly the confusion of throwing the shuttle."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Shimin, embraced him, and said, "Lately I had nearly fallen into the error of doubting a good son," alluding to the tale of Zeng Shen's mother.

sentences.zh: 世民跪而吮上乳，號慟久之。

translations.literal: Shimin knelt and sucked the emperor's breast, wailing grievously for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin knelt and pretended to nurse at the emperor's breast, weeping bitterly for a long while.

sentences.zh: 建成子安陸王承道、河東王承德、武安王承訓、汝南王承明、鉅鹿王承義，元吉子梁郡王承業、漁陽王承鸞、普安王承獎、江夏王承裕、義陽王承度，皆坐誅，仍絕屬籍。

translations.literal: Jiancheng's sons—the King of Anlu Chengdao, King of Hedong Chengde, King of Wu'an Chengxun, King of Runan Chengming, King of Julu Chengyi—and Yuanji's sons—the King of Liangjun Chengye, King of Yuyang Chengluan, King of Pu'an Chengjiang, King of Jiangxia Chengyu, King of Yiyang Chengdu—all sat for execution, and moreover were cut from the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: All of Jiancheng's sons—Kings of Anlu, Hedong, Wu'an, Runan, and Julu—and all of Yuanji's sons—Kings of Liangjun, Yuyang, Pu'an, Jiangxia, and Yiyang—were put to death and struck from the imperial clan rolls.

sentences.zh: 初，建成許元吉以正位之後，立為太弟，故元吉為之盡死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiancheng had promised Yuanji that after the proper succession he would be established as heir younger brother; therefore Yuanji for him gave his all unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiancheng had promised Yuanji that once he took the throne he would make him heir younger brother, and so Yuanji fought for him to the death.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲盡誅建成、元吉左右百餘人，籍沒其家，尉遲敬德固爭曰：「罪在二凶，既伏其誅；

translations.literal: The various generals wished to execute to the last Jiancheng's and Yuanji's attendants, more than a hundred men, and confiscate their households; Yuchi Jingde firmly argued: "Guilt lies with the two villains, who have already submitted to execution;
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to execute more than a hundred of Jiancheng's and Yuanji's retainers and confiscate their property; Yuchi Jingde argued firmly, "Guilt rests with the two villains, who have already been killed;

sentences.zh: 若及支黨，非所以求安也。」

translations.literal: if we reach to branches and factions, this is not the means to seek peace."
translations.idiomatic: to extend punishment to their followers is no way to secure peace."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: They then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They desisted.

sentences.zh: 是日，下詔赦天下。

translations.literal: That day, an edict was issued pardoning all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 凶逆之罪，止於建成、元吉，自餘黨與，一無所問。

translations.literal: Treacherous and rebellious guilt stopped at Jiancheng and Yuanji; from the rest of the party factions, none were questioned.
translations.idiomatic: The crimes of rebellion were confined to Jiancheng and Yuanji; all other associates were left unpunished.

sentences.zh: 其僧、尼、道士、女冠並宜仍舊。

translations.literal: Their monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and female Daoists should all remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and female Daoists were to continue as before.

sentences.zh: 國家庶事，皆取秦王處分。

translations.literal: The state's various affairs all took the Prince of Qin's disposal.
translations.idiomatic: All state business was to be handled by the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，馮立、謝叔方皆自出；

translations.literal: On xinyou, Feng Li and Xie Shufang both came out of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Feng Li and Xie Shufang both surrendered themselves;

sentences.zh: 薛萬徹亡匿，世民屢使諭之，乃出。

translations.literal: Xue Wanche hid in flight; Shimin several times sent messengers to instruct him, and he then came out.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wanche remained in hiding; Shimin sent messengers again and again to reassure him, and he finally gave himself up.

sentences.zh: 世民曰：「此皆忠於所事，義士也。」

translations.literal: Shimin said: "These all were loyal to whom they served—men of righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said, "These men were loyal to their masters—true men of honor."

sentences.zh: 釋之。

translations.literal: He released them.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，立世民為皇太子。

translations.literal: On guihai, Shimin was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Shimin was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「自今軍國庶事，無大小悉委太子處決，然後聞奏。」

translations.literal: Again an edict: "From now military and civil various affairs, none great or small, all are entrusted to the crown prince for decision, and only then reported up."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Henceforth all civil and military affairs, great and small, shall be decided by the crown prince, who shall report to me afterward."

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：立嫡以長，禮之正也。

translations.literal: Subject Guang said: Establishing the heir by senior legitimate birth is the orthodox of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Naming the eldest legitimate son as heir is the proper ritual order.

sentences.zh: 然高祖所以有天下，皆太宗之功；

translations.literal: Yet Gaozu's possessing all under Heaven was entirely the Taizong's achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Yet everything Gaozu won under Heaven was Taizong's doing;

sentences.zh: 隱太子以庸劣居其右，地嫌勢逼，必不相容。

translations.literal: the Hidden Crown Prince by mediocrity and inferiority occupied the superior place; territory suspicious and power pressing, they necessarily could not accommodate each other.
translations.idiomatic: the Hidden Crown Prince held precedence through birth alone, while merit and power pressed from below—such positions could not coexist.

sentences.zh: 向使高祖有文王之明，隱太子有泰伯之賢，太宗有子臧之節，則亂何自而生矣！

translations.literal: Had Gaozu possessed King Wen's clarity, the Hidden Crown Prince possessed Taibo's worth, and Taizong possessed Zizang's integrity, then from where would disorder have arisen of itself!
translations.idiomatic: Had Gaozu possessed King Wen's wisdom, the crown prince Taibo's virtue, and Taizong Zizang's selflessness, how could strife have arisen at all!

sentences.zh: 既不能然，太宗始欲俟其先發，然後應之，如此，則事非獲已，猶為愈也。

translations.literal: Unable to be so, Taizong at first wished to wait for them to move first, and then respond—thus the affair would not be obtained against one's will, and would still be better.
translations.idiomatic: That was impossible. Taizong at first wished to let them strike first and then answer in kind—still not ideal, but better.

sentences.zh: 既而為群下所迫，遂至蹀血禁門，推刃同氣，貽譏千古，惜哉！

translations.literal: Soon after he was compelled by the crowd below, and thereupon reached treading blood at the forbidden gate, thrusting blades against those of one womb, bequeathing ridicule for a thousand ages—pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his officers pressed him on, until blood was trampled at the palace gates and brother turned blade on brother—a stain on all ages. What a pity!

sentences.zh: 夫創業垂統之君，子孫之所儀刑也，彼中、明、肅、代之傳繼，得非有所指擬以為口實乎！

translations.literal: Now a lord who founds enterprise and hands down the standard—his descendants take him as model and law; those Zhongzong, Ruizong, Suzong, and Daizong successions—was it not that they had something to point to and take as mouth-real?
translations.idiomatic: Founders who establish dynasties set the pattern their heirs follow; did not the successions of Zhongzong, Ruizong, Suzong, and Daizong draw their justification from this very precedent?

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以宇文士及為太子詹事，長孫無忌、杜如晦為左庶子，高士廉、房玄齡為右庶子，尉遲敬德為左衛率，程知節為右衛率，虞世南為中舍人，褚亮為舍人，姚思廉為洗馬。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Yuwen Shiji was made crown prince household steward, Changsun Wuji and Du Ruhui were made left assistants to the heir, Gao Shilian and Fang Xuanling were made right assistants to the heir, Yuchi Jingde was made Left Weilü, Cheng Zhijie was made Right Weilü, Yu Shinan was made palace secretary, Chu Liang was made gentleman attendant, and Yao Silian was made study horse.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Yuwen Shiji was appointed crown prince household steward; Changsun Wuji and Du Ruhui were named left assistants to the heir; Gao Shilian and Fang Xuanling were named right assistants to the heir; Yuchi Jingde was made Left Weilü; Cheng Zhijie was made Right Weilü; Yu Shinan was made palace secretary; Chu Liang was made gentleman attendant; and Yao Silian was made study horse.

sentences.zh: 悉以齊王國司金帛什器賜敬德。

translations.literal: All took the Prince of Qi state office's gold, silks, and various utensils and bestowed them on Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: All the gold, silks, and furnishings of the Prince of Qi's household office were bestowed on Jingde.

sentences.zh: 初，洗馬魏徵常勸太子建成早除秦王，及建成敗，世民召徵謂曰：「汝何為離間我兄弟！」

translations.literal: Earlier, study horse Wei Zheng often urged crown prince Jiancheng early to eliminate the Prince of Qin; when Jiancheng was defeated, Shimin summoned Zheng and said: "Why did you divide and estrange my brothers!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Study Horse Wei Zheng had often urged Crown Prince Jiancheng to eliminate the Prince of Qin early; when Jiancheng fell, Shimin summoned him and said, "Why did you set my brothers against each other!"

sentences.zh: 眾為之危懼，徵舉止自若，對曰：「先太子早從徵言，必無今日之禍。」

translations.literal: The crowd for him was in peril and fear; Zheng's bearing and conduct were as if calm, and he replied: "Had the former crown prince early followed Zheng's words, there would necessarily be none of today's calamity."
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers feared for him, but Wei Zheng was perfectly composed and replied, "Had the late crown prince heeded my counsel in time, he would not have met today's fate."

sentences.zh: 世民素重其才，改容禮之，引為詹事主簿。

translations.literal: Shimin from of old valued his talent, changed countenance and honored him, and brought him in as household steward chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin had long valued his talent; his manner changed and he treated Wei Zheng with honor, appointing him chief clerk to the household steward.

sentences.zh: 亦召王珪、韋挺於巂州，皆以為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He also summoned Wang Gui and Wei Ting from Xizhou, and all were made admonishing and discussing grandees.
translations.idiomatic: He also recalled Wang Gui and Wei Ting from Xizhou and made them both Remonstrance and Discussion Grandees.

sentences.zh: 世民命縱禁苑鷹犬，罷四方貢獻，聽百官各陳治道，政令簡肅，中外大悅。

translations.literal: Shimin ordered to release the forbidden park's hawks and dogs, ceased tributes from the four quarters, listened to the hundred officials each stating governing ways; government orders were simple and austere; inside and outside were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin released the hunting birds and hounds from the imperial park, ended tribute missions from the provinces, invited officials to speak freely on governance, and simplified administration; court and country alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 以屈突通為陝東大行台左僕射，鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: He made Qutu Tong Eastern Shaanxi Grand Area Headquarters left vice director, garrisoning Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Qutu Tong left vice director of the Eastern Shaanxi Grand Metropolitan Prefecture, with his base at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 益州行台僕射竇軌與行台尚書韋雲起、郭行方不協。

translations.literal: Yizhou headquarters vice director Dou Gui did not get along with headquarters secretariat Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou Headquarters Vice Director Dou Gui was at odds with headquarters secretaries Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang.

sentences.zh: 雲起弟慶儉及宗族多事太子建成，建成死，軌誣雲起與建成同反，收斬之。

translations.literal: Yunqi's younger brother Qingjian and clan kin many served crown prince Jiancheng; when Jiancheng died, Gui falsely charged Yunqi with joining Jiancheng in rebellion, arrested and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi's brother Qingjian and many of his kin had served Crown Prince Jiancheng; after Jiancheng's death, Dou Gui accused Yunqi of rebelling with him, had him arrested, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 行方懼，逃奔京師，軌追之，不及。

translations.literal: Xingfang was afraid, fled running to the capital; Gui pursued him but did not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xingfang fled to the capital in fear; Dou Gui pursued but could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾寇岷州。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun raided Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun raided Min Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇隴州；

translations.literal: The Turks raided Longzhou;
translations.idiomatic: The Turks raided Long Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 辛未，寇渭州。

translations.literal: On xinwei, they raided Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, they raided Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遣右衛大將軍柴紹擊之。

translations.literal: The court sent Right Guard grand general Chai Shao to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Right Guard Grand General Chai Shao to attack them.

sentences.zh: 廢益州大行台，置大都督府。

translations.literal: The Yizhou Grand Area Headquarters was abolished and a Grand Area Commander headquarters was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Yizhou Grand Metropolitan Prefecture was abolished and a grand area commander headquarters was established.

sentences.zh: 壬申，上以手詔賜裴寂等曰：「朕當加尊號為太上皇。」

translations.literal: On renshen, the emperor with a hand edict bestowed on Pei Ji and others, saying: "I shall add honored title as Retired Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the emperor sent a hand edict to Pei Ji and the others, saying, "I shall take the honored title of Retired Emperor."

sentences.zh: 辛巳，幽州大都督廬江王瑗反，右領軍將軍王君廓殺之，傳首。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Youzhou Grand Area Commander King of Lujiang Yuan rebelled; Right Leading Army General Wang Jun'guo killed him and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Youzhou Grand Area Commander Li Yuan, King of Lujiang, rebelled; Right Leading Army General Wang Jun'guo killed him and sent his head.

sentences.zh: 初，上以瑗懦怯非將帥才，使君廓佐之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor because Yuan was timid and cowardly, not a commander-in-chief's talent, had Jun'guo assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, judging Yuan timid and unfit for command, the emperor had Jun'guo assist him.

sentences.zh: 君廓故群盜，勇悍險詐，瑗推心倚伏之，許為昏姻。

translations.literal: Jun'guo was formerly of the bandit groups, brave, fierce, dangerous and deceitful; Yuan opened his heart and relied on him, promising marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Jun'guo had been a bandit chief, brave, fierce, and treacherous; Yuan trusted him completely and promised him a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 太子建成謀害秦王，密與瑗相結。

translations.literal: Crown prince Jiancheng plotted to harm the Prince of Qin and secretly joined with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jiancheng had plotted against the Prince of Qin and secretly allied with Yuan.

sentences.zh: 建成死，詔遣通事舍人崔敦禮馳驛召瑗。

translations.literal: Jiancheng died; an edict sent Communications Gentleman Cui Dunli by urgent relay to summon Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiancheng's death, an edict sent Communications Gentleman Cui Dunli by urgent relay to summon Yuan.

sentences.zh: 瑗心不自安，謀於君廓。

translations.literal: Yuan's heart was not at ease and he plotted with Jun'guo.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was uneasy and took counsel with Jun'guo.

sentences.zh: 君廓欲取瑗以為功，乃說曰：「大王若入，必無全理。

translations.literal: Jun'guo wished to take Yuan for merit and therefore urged: "Great King, if you enter, there will necessarily be no intact principle.
translations.idiomatic: Jun'guo wished to win merit by betraying him and urged, "Great King, if you go to court, you will surely not come back alive.

sentences.zh: 今擁兵為數萬，奈何受單使之召，自投罔罟乎！」

translations.literal: Now you hold troops numbering in the tens of thousands—how can you accept a lone envoy's summons and cast yourself into the net trap!"
translations.idiomatic: You command tens of thousands of men—how can you answer a lone envoy's summons and walk into the net yourself!"

sentences.zh: 因相與泣。

translations.literal: They thereupon wept together.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together.

sentences.zh: 瑗曰：「我今以命托公，舉事決矣。」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "I now entrust my life to you, sir—the undertaking is decided."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "I now entrust my life to you—the deed is decided."

sentences.zh: 乃劫敦禮，問以京師機事；

translations.literal: He then seized Dunli and questioned him on the capital's confidential affairs;
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Dunli and questioned him about affairs in the capital;

sentences.zh: 敦禮不屈，瑗囚之，發驛徵兵，且召燕州剌史王詵赴薊，與之計事。

translations.literal: Dunli would not bend; Yuan imprisoned him, sent relay posts to levy troops, and moreover summoned Yanzhou inspector Wang Shen to Ji to plan affairs with him.
translations.idiomatic: Dunli would not yield; Yuan imprisoned him, called up troops by relay post, and summoned Yan Prefecture inspector Wang Shen to Ji to plan with him.

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍王利涉說瑗曰：「王君廓反覆，不可委以機柄，宜早除去，以王詵代之。」

translations.literal: Army caocan Wang Lishe urged Yuan: "Wang Jun'guo is changeable and unreliable; you cannot entrust him with the crucial handle—you ought early to remove him and replace him with Wang Shen."
translations.idiomatic: Army Caocan Wang Lishe urged Yuan, "Wang Jun'guo is treacherous and cannot be trusted with command; you should remove him early and put Wang Shen in his place."

sentences.zh: 瑗不能決。

translations.literal: Yuan could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan could not decide.

sentences.zh: 君廓知之，往見詵，詵方沐，握髮而出，君廓手斬之，持其首告眾曰：「李瑗與王詵同反，囚執敕使，擅自徵兵。

translations.literal: Jun'guo knew it, went to see Shen; Shen was just bathing, grasped his hair and came out; Jun'guo with his hand beheaded him, held his head and announced to the masses: "Li Yuan and Wang Shen together rebelled, imprisoned and seized the edict envoy, on their own authority levied troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jun'guo learned of it, went to see Shen, who was bathing and came out clutching his hair; Jun'guo cut off his head with his own hand, held it up, and told the troops, "Li Yuan and Wang Shen have rebelled together, imprisoned the imperial envoy, and levied troops on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 今詵已誅，獨有李瑗，無能為也。

translations.literal: Now Shen is already executed; alone there is Li Yuan, who can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen is already dead; only Li Yuan remains, and he can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 汝寧隨瑗族滅乎，欲從我以取富貴乎？」

translations.literal: Would you rather follow Yuan and clan be exterminated, or wish to follow me to take wealth and honor?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you follow Yuan to ruin with his clan, or follow me to wealth and honor?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆曰：「願從公討賊。」

translations.literal: All said: "We wish to follow you, sir, to punish the rebel."
translations.idiomatic: All cried, "We will follow you to punish the traitor!"

sentences.zh: 君廓乃帥其麾下千餘人，逾西城而入，瑗不之覺；

translations.literal: Jun'guo then led his subordinates, more than a thousand men, crossed the west wall and entered; Yuan did not notice it;
translations.idiomatic: Jun'guo then led more than a thousand of his men over the west wall into the city before Yuan knew it;

sentences.zh: 君廓入獄出敦禮，瑗始知之，遽帥左右數百人被甲而出，遇君廓於門外。

translations.literal: Jun'guo entered the prison and released Dunli; Yuan then learned of it, hurriedly led several hundred men at left and right in armor and came out, meeting Jun'guo outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jun'guo freed Dunli from prison; Yuan learned of it, hurried out in armor with several hundred men, and met Jun'guo at the gate.

sentences.zh: 君廓謂瑗眾曰：「李瑗為逆，汝何為隨之入湯火乎！」

translations.literal: Jun'guo said to Yuan's masses: "Li Yuan is rebellious—why do you follow him into boiling water and fire!"
translations.idiomatic: Jun'guo called to Yuan's men, "Li Yuan is a rebel—why follow him into fire and ruin!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆棄兵而潰。

translations.literal: All discarded weapons and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: They threw down their weapons and fled.

sentences.zh: 唯瑗獨存，罵君廓曰：「小人賣我，行自及矣！」

translations.literal: Only Yuan alone remained, cursed Jun'guo: "Petty man, you sold me out—you will soon reach yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Only Yuan was left. He cursed Jun'guo, "You wretch sold me out—you will get yours in turn!"

sentences.zh: 遂執瑗，縊之。

translations.literal: He then seized Yuan and strangled him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yuan and strangled him.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以王君廓為左領軍大將軍兼幽州都督，以瑗家口賜之。

translations.literal: On renwu, Wang Jun'guo was made Left Leading Army Grand General and concurrently Youzhou area commander; Yuan's household mouths were bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Wang Jun'guo was made Left Leading Army Grand General and concurrently Youzhou area commander; Yuan's household was given to him as spoils.

sentences.zh: 敦禮，仲方之孫也。

translations.literal: Dunli was Zhongfang's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Dunli was a grandson of Cui Zhongfang.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，罷天策府。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the Heavenly Stratagem headquarters was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the Heavenly Stratagem headquarters was abolished.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己丑，柴紹破突厥於秦州，斬特勒一人，士卒首千餘級。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, Chai Shao defeated the Turks at Qinzhou, beheaded one Tiele man, more than a thousand heads of soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, Chai Shao defeated the Turks at Qin Prefecture, beheaded one Tiele chieftain, and took more than a thousand enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 以秦府護軍秦叔寶為左衛大將軍，又以程知節為右武衛大將軍，尉遲敬德為右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: Took Qin palace guard commander Qin Shubao as Left Guard grand general; again took Cheng Zhijie as Right Martial Guard grand general, Yuchi Jingde as Right Martial Tiger grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shubao of the Prince of Qin's guard was made Left Guard Grand General; Cheng Zhijie was made Right Martial Guard Grand General, and Yuchi Jingde Right Martial Tiger Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以高士廉為侍中，房玄齡為中書令，蕭瑀為左僕射，長孫無忌為吏部尚書，杜如晦為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On renchen, took Gao Shilian as palace attendant, Fang Xuanling as secretariat director, Xiao Yu as left vice director, Zhangsun Wuji as Ministry of Personnel minister, Du Ruhui as Ministry of War minister.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Gao Shilian was made Palace Attendant, Fang Xuanling Secretariat Director, Xiao Yu Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Zhangsun Wuji Minister of Personnel, and Du Ruhui Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以宇文士及為中書令，封德彝為右僕射；

translations.literal: On guisi, took Yuwen Shiji as secretariat director, Feng Deyi as right vice director;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Yuwen Shiji was made Secretariat Director and Feng Deyi Right Vice Director;

sentences.zh: 又以前天策府兵曹參軍杜淹為御史大夫，中書舍人顏師古、劉林甫為中書侍郎，左衛副率侯君集為左衛將軍，左虞候段志玄為驍衛將軍，副護軍薛萬徹為右領軍將軍，右內副率張公謹為右武候將軍，右監門率長孫安業為右監門將軍，右內副率李客師為領左右軍將軍。

translations.literal: Again took the former Heavenly Strategies Bureau army-camp registrar Du Yan as censor-in-chief; secretariat drafting officers Yan Shigu and Liu Linpu as secretariat vice directors; Left Guard deputy commander Hou Junji as Left Guard general; Left Brilliant Reedward Duan Zhixuan as Valiant Guard general; deputy guard commander Xue Wanche as Right Leading Army general; Right Inner deputy commander Zhang Gongjin as Right Martial Tiger general; Right Palace Gate deputy commander Zhangsun Anye as Right Palace Gate general; Right Inner deputy commander Li Keshi as commander of the Left and Right Personal Guard armies.
translations.idiomatic: also the former Heavenly Strategies Bureau army-camp registrar Du Yan was made Censor-in-Chief; Secretariat drafting officers Yan Shigu and Liu Linpu were made Secretariat vice directors; Left Guard deputy commander Hou Junji was made Left Guard general; Left Brilliant Reedward section chief Duan Zhixuan was made Valiant Guard general; deputy guard commander Xue Wanche was made Right Leading Army general; Right Inner deputy commander Zhang Gongjin was made Right Martial Tiger Guard general; Right Palace Gate deputy commander Zhangsun Anye was made Right Palace Gate general; and Right Inner deputy commander Li Keshi was made commander of the Left and Right Personal Guard armies.

sentences.zh: 安業，無忌之兄；

translations.literal: Anye was Wuji's elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: Anye was Zhangsun Wuji's elder brother;

sentences.zh: 客師，靖之弟也。

translations.literal: Keshi was Jing's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Keshi was Li Jing's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 太子建成、齊王元吉之黨散亡在民間，雖更赦令，猶不自安，徼幸者爭告捕以邀賞。

translations.literal: Crown prince Jiancheng's and Prince of Qi Yuanji's partisans scattered and lost among the people; though amnesties were renewed, they still were not at ease; those seeking advantage vied to report and capture for reward.
translations.idiomatic: The partisans of the late Crown Prince Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Yuanji who had scattered among the people, though amnestied again and again, were still uneasy; opportunists vied to denounce and capture them for reward.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫王珪以啟太子。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and discussion grand master Wang Gui thereby reported to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master Wang Gui reported this to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丙子，太子下令：「六月四日已前事連東宮及齊王，十七日前連李瑗者，並不得相告言，違者反坐。」

translations.literal: On bingzi, the crown prince issued an order: "Matters before the fourth day of the sixth month that touch the Eastern Palace and the Prince of Qi, and before the seventeenth day that touch Li Yuan, all must not be reported to one another; violators suffer counter-penalty."
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the crown prince issued an order: "Matters before the fourth day of the sixth month that touch on the Eastern Palace or the Prince of Qi, and before the seventeenth day that touch on Li Yuan, must not be denounced; violators shall be punished under the counter-accusation law."

sentences.zh: 丁酉，遣諫議大夫魏徵宣慰山東，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: On dingyou, sent remonstrance and discussion grand master Wei Zheng to proclaim comfort in Shandong, listening to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the court sent Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master Wei Zheng to proclaim comfort in the Shandong region, with authority to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 徵至磁州，遇州縣錮送前太子千牛李志安、齊王護軍李師行詣京師，徵曰：「吾受命之日，前宮、齊府左右皆赦不問；
